Question #6 in our "One Hard Question" series. "Least privilege" gets harder with agents because access is only half the story. A reporting agent may legitimately have storage access and still have no reason to invoke Delete. The control has to understand not just what the agent can access, but what actions make sense for the task it is performing right now. How is your team enforcing least privilege at the action level? Agree with this. The goal is not to choose between innovation and governance. The goal is to make AI useful without losing accountability. As Agentic systems move into healthcare, finance, public services, and daily work, oversight needs to be real: who is responsible, when does someone step in, and how do we know the guardrails actually worked? Trust will come from answering these questions.

I'm excited to introduce Polymath Society. Your resume and LinkedIn do not know who you really are. But your AI tools do. Polymath helps you analyze your Claude Code/Codex/Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, and Notion logs. If Polymath thinks you're good, you can share a condensed, privacy-safe report with us and we will get you opportunities directly in your inbox. OpenAI is thinking about this the right way. Production agents need more than a capable model. They need policies, evaluations, controls, and continuous validation around them. At CompFly AI , we believe trust should attach to the agent and its job, not to a model provider. We are building a model-agnostic trust layer for agents, so enterprises can use the best model for each task and change models without rebuilding confidence from scratch. #AIAgents #EnterpriseAI #AgentSecurity

Some people make you hope the first time you build together won’t be the last. Jason is one of those people. At Rivian, I saw Jason take on ambitious problems that spanned platforms, products, and teams, and turn them into systems people could depend on. He also has a rare ability to build strong teams that do exceptional work and have a lot of fun doing it together. That’s why I’m incredibly excited to share that Jason Shiverick is joining CompFly AI as CTO. We’re building CompFly around a question that every company adopting agents will need to answer: How do I know I can trust this agent with this task? Not just whether an agent can create an impressive demo, but whether it can be given real responsibility inside a business, with confidence. Jason’s addition makes CompFly stronger than ever, and I couldn’t be happier about the team taking shape with Anand Salodkar , Prakash Narayanamoorthy , Nikhil Anirudh N. , and everyone building alongside us. Round two, Jason. This one is going to be fun So much more to come :)

As AI agents delegate work across other agents, tools, and memory, authority can drift far beyond the original instruction. CompFly AI 's CEO Venkat Siva (Sivasubramanian) explains why this “transitive delegation” is becoming a critical enterprise risk and why access controls alone are not enough. https://lnkd.in/gS-zUN3k
